thread:
maria.powell: FYI customer (payment rails startup) reports garbled JSON after reconnecting their SSE stream. They say the stream is fine until they hit a network blip, then on reconnect the next messages are malformed or arrive out of order.

samir.kapoor: rough repro steps? SDK/lang?

maria.powell: Using our Python SDK v0.12.3 async iterator behind a flaky mobile proxy; they do token rotation on reconnect. Also tried client-side TS SDK v1.4.0 and saw slightly different behavior.

ingrid.nelson: can you paste the minimal repro or logs?

maria.powell: customer pasted logs. here's an excerpt:
```
... 2026-03-14T18:22:10.123Z INFO SSE connected
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.001Z WARN connection dropped (ETIMEDOUT)
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.002Z INFO reauth token rotate
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.100Z INFO SSE reconnect attempt
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.150Z INFO SSE EVENT chunk: "{\"choices\": [{\"delta\": {\"content\": \"Hello, \", \"role\": \"assistant\"}}]}"
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.151Z INFO SSE EVENT chunk: "\"content\": \"world!\"}] }\n"
... 2026-03-14T18:22:14.152Z ERROR json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 75 (char 74)
```

maria.powell: So they get two adjacent chunks where the boundary lands inside a JSON token and the join produces malformed JSON. They think the server re-sent a tail fragment and client appended it incorrectly.

jason.wu: interesting. Does the server send chunk framing metadata (seq id / offset)? we added resume tokens in the runtime last quarter.

ingrid.nelson: Yes, the runtime now attaches an id header "x-stream-offset" and a resume token cookie when available, but older code paths don't always emit both. I suspect a race: reconnect path streams cached buffered partial frame then also resumes and replays the remainder.

samir.kapoor: repro on our side: I ran a local proxy that cut connection for 200ms and reconnected. Python SDK async iterator (await for chunk) behaves like this: after reconnect it yields an empty string item, then resumes with the next chunk — client code was naive and concatenated items, producing the same broken JSON. TS SDK instead replays the last nonterminal chunk, so you get duplicated fragments. Both lead to parse errors.

maria.powell: customer also reported billing duplicate consumption for the replayed tokens. billing-bot will want a look. @billing-bot can you comment?

billing-bot: flagged. If server-side replay causes identical tokens to be counted twice before dedupe window expires, we may have an exposure. Need to correlate session_id + resume_token + timestamps.

jason.wu: from runtime traces I see this timeline: connect -> partial frame buffered (prefix) -> connection loss -> runtime marks stream as "interrupted" and starts resume -> resume logic pulls the buffered prefix and sends it downstream while the reconnect path also replays from checkpoint. Essentially double-send of overlapping fragments.

maria.powell: customer workaround request — they want a quick mitigation we can advise.

ingrid.nelson: short-term workaround: 1) in Python SDK set iterator to coalesce chunks only after filtering out empty items and de-duplicating by checking for overlapping suffix/prefix heuristics, 2) in TS recommend enabling strict resume header check and abort/restart stream on token rotation. Not ideal but buys time.

jason.wu: we should push a hotfix to the runtime: ensure that resume path either uses a deterministic checkpoint (byte offset) and never emits a cached partial fragment twice, or tag replayed fragments with a boundary marker so clients can reassemble safely.

maria.powell: can you write a repro harness and a unit test? customer is having production impact.

jason.wu: will do. quick plan: I’ll add an integration test that simulates partial-frame buffer + reconnect, assert the server emits exactly one canonical reassembled JSON event. Also add guards in the resume code to drop cached partial fragment if resume from checkpoint > 0.

samir.kapoor: SDK changes: Python iterator should treat consecutive empty/whitespace chunks as "incomplete" and wait for a terminal newline before yielding to user. TS SDK should include an internal sequence ID and ignore replays with identical seq id already processed.

maria.powell: customer asked for repro steps we can run. here's what they used (simplified):
```
# start a simple SSE server that splits messages mid-token
python3 -m http.server 8080 &
# client uses proxy that kills socket for 150-300ms at random
# run python sdk example (async iterator) against the proxy
```
I'll paste full snippet later.

ingrid.nelson: I’m seeing a recent deploy (canary) that touched streaming buffer code. @deploy-bot any recent deploys around 18:20 UTC?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy r-2026-03-14-18:15 applied to streaming-runtime workers. No immediate rollback.

maria.powell: ok that aligns with the customer incident time. Can we rollback the canary while we patch?

jason.wu: request rollback approved. rolling back canary now.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for r-2026-03-14-18:15 -> target state r-2026-03-14-17:50. ETA 90s.

ops-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-0314-57 assigned to eng-runtime. Priority P1.

maria.powell: I'll tell customer we're investigating, asking for their session IDs and sample raw SSE fragments. Also gave them workaround to restart stream on token rotation for now.

samir.kapoor: followups: 1) add E2E test for partial-fragment + reconnect, 2) add server-side dedupe by session_id+seq, 3) add SDK idempotency check and better iterator semantics, 4) billing to run dedupe window calculation to refund if duplicate billed tokens found.

jason.wu: will open PRs for runtime and SDK. tagging QA and customer success.

maria.powell: thanks — customer is waiting for ETA. I’ll update thread when rollback done and when we have a patched canary. :pray:

ingrid.nelson: quick note for support playbook: if customer sees json.decoder.JSONDecodeError after reconnect, ask them to capture raw SSE lines (not just assembled messages) and session/resume headers. That will help identify double-send vs client-assembly bug.

maria.powell: added to support playbook.

jason.wu: PRs: runtime fix (WIP) and python-sdk iterator change (WIP). will ping once canary validated.

maria.powell: closing loop with customer — will update in 30 minutes.
